text:
B: Oh hello! Can you hear me? Sorry, I never know if these things are actually working.
A: Yeah, no, I can hear you fine. Hiya. I'm Rhys.
B: Lisa. Nice to meet you, Rhys. How did you get on with that puzzle thing at the start? I was useless, me. I think I got about three.
A: Erm, the puzzle... yeah, I sort of panicked on the number ones. The shape ones were all right, I think. Not sure.
B: See, I'm the other way round, I'm fine with numbers 'cause I do bookings all day, but the shapes, I just sat there going, what am I looking at?
A: That's fair. What sort of bookings?
B: Freight, so shipping containers. I work for a little freight forwarding firm near Felixstowe, the port. I do all the paperwork, chase the customs documents, answer the phones. Sounds dead boring when I say it out loud, but it's actually quite busy, you never know what's going to go wrong on a Monday.
A: No, that doesn't sound boring. Sounds stressful, if anything.
B: It can be! Somebody's container's stuck and they're shouting at me like I'm personally holding it. What about you, what do you do?
A: Erm, I'm a video editor. Senior editor, at an agency in Cardiff. So it's mostly corporate films, social ads, that sort of thing. Bit of motion graphics. And the odd sort of telly-adjacent job, which is the fun bit.
B: Ooh, that's clever. I said to myself when I saw your picture, he looks like one of the IT boys at work. Clever, but quiet. Sorry, that sounds rude!
A: No, no, that's fair, that's probably accurate, to be honest.
B: Is that a dog bed I saw in the corner of yours?
A: It is, yeah. Moss. She's a whippet, a rescue. She's lovely but she's terrified of everything. She won't walk past the wheelie bins on bin day, like, she just stops dead and shakes. So I have to carry her past them. Every fortnight. Which, sorry, I'm rambling.
B: No, I love that! We've got Bramble, she's a Staffy, getting on a bit now and a bit chunky. She's snoring on the sofa right now, actually, you might hear her. She's scared of nothing, she'd walk straight into a bin. She'd probably try and eat it.
A: Ha. Opposite problems.
B: So where's Moss walked, then, are you in Cardiff?
A: Caerphilly, just outside. We go up Caerphilly Mountain most weekends. It's not really a mountain, it's more of a big hill, but don't tell anyone round here I said that.
B: Your secret's safe. We just do the park or along the river. Christchurch Park. I keep saying I'll do one of those Couch to 5K things and then I don't.
A: I bought a road bike in lockdown. It's in the garage. That's sort of the same story.
B: Oh, everyone did that! My husband Dean bought a rowing machine. It's a clothes horse now.
A: Yeah, mine's basically a very expensive coat hook. Erm, do you commute far, then, to Felixstowe?
B: Half hour, on a good day. The A14's a nightmare though, there's always something. Lorries, obviously, 'cause of the port. You?
A: The A469 into Cardiff. It's, yeah. On deadline days I'm having a pint of coffee by nine just to cope with the drive.
B: A pint of coffee! You'll be shaking like your dog.
A: That's, yeah, honestly, that's not far off.
B: Do you like it, though, the editing? It must be nice making something you can actually see at the end.
A: Erm, yeah, I do. I think when it's a good project it's the best job going, you know, getting the pacing right, the colour. The corporate stuff can be a bit, erm, it's a lot of people in fleeces talking about synergy. But I did one last year for a
